title: Logarithmic Las Vegas dynamic connectivity
formal: Does an always-correct Las Vegas word-RAM data structure maintain connectivity of an initially empty undirected simple graph on \([n]\) with \(O(\log(2+n))\) amortized expected time per edge update and \(O(\log(2+n))\) worst-case time per query, using \(O((n+m)\log^c(2+n))\) words for some fixed \(c\), where \(m\) is the current number of edges?
definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. Here \(w=\lceil a\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) for a fixed constant \(a\) sufficient to address the allowed space. Insert adds a missing edge; Delete removes a present edge; Connected(u,v) returns whether a path joins the two supplied vertices. Valid operations form any finite sequence fixed independently of the random bits. The expected total cost is \(O(n\log^c(2+n)+(u+q)\log(2+n))\) for \(u\) updates and \(q\) queries; the first term includes initialization from the empty graph. Every individual query must meet its worst-case bound. Every answer is correct, and all operations terminate almost surely. This asks for amortized expected updates against an oblivious adversary, not deterministic or worst-case update guarantees. The algorithm has no advance access to future updates.
why: Closing the remaining iterated-logarithm gap would pin down a central dynamic graph primitive near its information-theoretic lower bounds.

context_blocks.text: The 2023 Las Vegas structure has \(O(\log n(\log\log n)^2)\) amortized expected update time and \(O(\log n/\log\log\log n)\) worst-case queries.
Polylogarithmic worst-case connectivity is a separate research direction: a larger polylogarithm per operation does not provide logarithmic amortized update time.

progress.text: The Las Vegas amortized bound comes within a squared logarithmic-logarithmic factor of logarithmic updates.
The expected worst-case polylogarithmic result concerns a different quantitative guarantee.

sentences: An undirected graph changes one edge at a time.
A query asks whether two vertices remain connected.
The target is logarithmic amortized expected update time with always-correct answers.
Known Las Vegas bounds retain an iterated-logarithm overhead.
The related deterministic worst-case problem asks for different guarantees.
